rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a very poor-quality early blastocyst and correctly notes absent/degenerative ICM and TE, but it misstates expansion grade 1 as <50% despite the provided definition saying blastocoel at least half the embryo, and adds some image-specific details that may be overinterpreted.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, male factor, sperm parameters, BMI, endometrium, and first-cycle status with embryo quality reasonably well, though some links (stress, sedentary lifestyle, former smoking) are more speculative than central.

The reasoning is mostly logical and internally consistent: very poor morphology drives a very low implantation estimate despite otherwise decent patient factors. Minor issues include overconfidence about causes and some extrapolation from limited data.

Mostly aligned in recognizing 1DD as very poor prognosis and suggesting counseling, but statements like many labs would not transfer, recommending compassionate transfer framing, and suggesting IMSI/PICSI as optimization are not strongly guideline-based; the endometrium being 'trilaminar likely' is also unsupported.

Provides clear options for transfer versus no transfer, counseling points, and future workup ideas such as sperm DNA fragmentation testing and lifestyle optimization. It is practical, though some recommendations are not strongly evidence-based and the future plan is truncated.
